endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Document who owns the intake process, how it is communicated to staff, and how compliance is monitored.

endorsements.title: Health Equity Across the AI Lifecycle (HEAAL) framework
endorsements.issuer: Health AI Partnership; PLOS Digital Health (PMID 38723025, doi:10.1371/journal.pdig.0000390)
endorsements.quote: While all standard procedures should be applied to all AI solutions of interest, some procedures are tested at different decision points or follow a different sequential order based on whether the solutions already exist or not.

endorsements.title: Operationalizing the EU AI Act in a comprehensive cancer center through an institutional governance framework
endorsements.quote: It operates as a single point of entry for Data/AI initiatives, bringing together institutional leadership, information systems, the project office, the data prote ction officer, and clinical and medico -technical functions.

endorsements.title: A practical framework for appropriate implementation and review of artificial intelligence (FAIR-AI) in healthcare
endorsements.quote: As the first step in FAIR-AI, an AI solution needs to go through an intake process.

endorsements.title: Clinical use of artificial intelligence requires AI-capable organizations
endorsements.quote: For example, personnel responsible for assessment of proposed AI tools can use a standardized protocol to evaluate the sponsorship, quality, performance, and planned use of every AI tool, whether it is a relatively minor feature built into a radiological device or a predictive risk scoring tool that will impact patient triage and care.

endorsements.title: AI ethics for the everyday intensivist
endorsements.issuer: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
endorsements.quote: These mechanisms should also be implemented at the organisational level, and may include embedding the reporting of AI tools to existing safety and quality improvement committees and ensuring procurement processes are redesigned to enable robust evaluation of the AI technology.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence and Enhanced Recovery After Surgery as Patient Safety Strategies for Perioperative Care in Resource-Limited Settings
endorsements.quote: Hospitals should avoid purchasing isolated digital tools that are not connected to ERAS pathways, escalation protocols, staff training, patient safety metrics, and accountability structures.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence in echocardiography: a position statement from the British Society of Echocardiography
endorsements.quote: Furthermore, local governance processes will need to be followed, including assessment and approval by local policies regardless of the healthcare setting.

endorsements.title: AI as Core Infrastructure in Radiology: Moving Beyond Pilots to Operational Excellence
endorsements.issuer: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
endorsements.quote: First, there is a single intake path.

endorsements.title: The VIBE-HI framework: a conceptual model for evaluating vibe coding appropriateness, quality, and safety in health informatics
endorsements.quote: First, an intake and triage form on which a clinician scores a proposed tool against the four Layer-1 criteria and routes it to a clinical-informatics or AI-governance committee; the form yields a tier and a role in minutes.

endorsements.title: When end users can build: AI-assisted application development and the new accountability gap in digital health
endorsements.quote: A better response is to create clearer pathways for review, triage, and support.

endorsements.title: Building Clinical Artificial Intelligence at the PICU Bedside: Recognizing the Clinician-Builder
endorsements.quote: When institutions provide no governed pathway, clinicians improvise, already using consumer-grade frontier models for documentation, differentials, and patient communication without oversight ( 10 – 12 ).

commentary.bottom_line: Ten sources endorse a single structured intake and governance review for all AI tools, including procured, embedded vendor, and legacy tools, but no supplied study tests whether such review reduces unreviewed AI use or patient harm. The recommendation rests on framework and commentary consensus, and no supplied study documents the hazard either.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests the practice, and none measures how often AI enters use through procurement or vendor updates without review. The ten endorsements consist of two frameworks and eight commentaries. Under GRADE conventions, expert opinion does not count as evidence of effect, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

The endorsements describe a plausible failure mode in which embedded or updated vendor features reach clinical use without anyone assessing them. No supplied study measures how often this happens, what harm follows, or whether a central intake catches such tools before they affect patients. The safety benefit therefore remains an untested expectation.

One commentary proposes an intake form that yields a risk tier in minutes, and another describes clinicians building tools outside any governed pathway. Neither claim comes with workflow data. No supplied study reports intake completion rates, review turnaround, staff burden, or whether clinicians route tools through intake once it exists.

The HEAAL framework calls for applying standard procedures to all AI tools, whether they already exist or are proposed. No supplied study examines whether a single intake process surfaces equity concerns for tools used with Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients.

commentary.research_gap: Studies should compare health systems with and without a single intake process on the share of AI tools in use that received documented review, the time from vendor update to review, reviewer staffing costs, and downstream safety events tied to unreviewed tools. A baseline audit of how many embedded and legacy AI features currently operate without review would also establish the size of the hazard.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice in any population, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy settings. One commentary addresses resource-limited settings but reports no data. Safety-net systems may carry more legacy and vendor-embedded tools with fewer governance staff, and whether a single intake process is feasible or effective there is unknown.
